# 1 Samuel Chapter 16 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 159r–159v | **Source Image:** 1SA_016_page_001.jpg, 1SA_016_page_002.jpg

---

**16:1** And the LORD said to Samuel, "How long will you mourn for Saul, seeing I have rejected him from reigning over Israel? Fill your horn with oil and go. I am sending you to Jesse the Bethlehemite, for I have provided for Myself a king among his sons."

**16:2** And Samuel said, "How can I go? If Saul hears of it, he will kill me." And the LORD said, "Take a heifer with you and say, 'I have come to sacrifice to the LORD.'

**16:3** And you shall call Jesse to the sacrifice, and I will make known to you what you shall do, and you shall anoint for Me the one I indicate to you."

**16:4** And Samuel did what the LORD spoke, and he came to Bethlehem. And the elders of the city came trembling to meet him and said, "Do you come in peace?"

**16:5** And he said, "In peace. I have come to sacrifice to the LORD. Consecrate yourselves and come with me to the sacrifice." And he consecrated Jesse and his sons and called them to the sacrifice.

**16:6** And when they came, he looked upon Eliab and thought, "Surely the LORD's anointed stands before Him."

**16:7** But the LORD said to Samuel, "Do not look upon his appearance or the height of his stature, for I have rejected him. For the LORD does not see as man sees; man looks upon the outward appearance, but the LORD looks upon the heart."

**16:8** Then Jesse called Abinadab and made him pass before Samuel. And he said, "Neither has the LORD chosen this one."

**16:9** Then Jesse made Shammah pass by. And he said, "Neither has the LORD chosen this one."

**16:10** And Jesse made seven of his sons pass before Samuel. And Samuel said to Jesse, "The LORD has not chosen these."

**16:11** Then Samuel said to Jesse, "Are these all the young men?" And he said, "There remains yet the youngest, and behold, he is tending the sheep." And Samuel said to Jesse, "Send for him, for we will not sit down until he comes."

**16:12** And he sent and brought him in. Now he was ruddy, with beautiful eyes and a handsome appearance. And the LORD said, "Arise, anoint him, for this is the one."

**16:13** And Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the midst of his brothers. And the Spirit of the LORD rushed upon David from that day forward. Then Samuel rose and went to Ramah.

**16:14** Now the Spirit of the LORD had departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from the LORD tormented him.

**16:15** And Saul's servants said to him, "Behold, an evil spirit from God is tormenting you.

**16:16** Let our lord now command your servants who are before you to seek out a man who is skilled in playing the lyre. And when the evil spirit from God is upon you, he will play, and it will be well with you."

**16:17** And Saul said to his servants, "Find me a man who plays well and bring him to me."

**16:18** And one of the young men answered and said, "Behold, I have seen a son of Jesse the Bethlehemite who is skilled in playing, a mighty man of valor, a man of war, prudent in speech, a man of fine appearance, and the LORD is with him."

**16:19** So Saul sent messengers to Jesse and said, "Send me David your son, who is with the sheep."

**16:20** And Jesse took a donkey laden with bread, a skin of wine, and a young goat, and sent them by the hand of David his son to Saul.

**16:21** And David came to Saul and entered his service. And Saul loved him greatly, and David became his armor-bearer.

**16:22** And Saul sent word to Jesse, saying, "Let David remain in my service, for he has found favor in my sight."

**16:23** And whenever the spirit from God was upon Saul, David would take the lyre and play. And there would be relief for Saul, and it would be well with him, and the evil spirit would depart from him.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

All three translators agreed substantially on the following:
- **16:4–5**: The trembling of the elders and Samuel's reassurance of peace were rendered consistently across all versions.
- **16:8–10**: The sequential rejection of Jesse's sons was translated with near-identical phrasing by all three.
- **16:12**: All agreed on "ruddy" for *admoni*, "beautiful eyes," and "handsome appearance," with only minor syntactic variation.
- **16:13**: All three preserved "horn of oil," "in the midst of his brothers," and the Spirit rushing upon David. EMET and LOGOS both used "rushed upon"; PNEUMA paraphrased as "came upon David with power" — SOPHIA retains "rushed upon" for its closer correspondence to *tsalchah*.
- **16:19–20**: The sending of David with gifts was rendered identically in substance.
- **16:21**: All agreed David became Saul's armor-bearer and that Saul loved him.

---
## Disagreement Log

**16:1** — *Verb for God's choice*
- EMET: "I have seen among his sons for Me a king" (preserving *ra'iti*)
- LOGOS: "I have provided for Myself a king among his sons"
- PNEUMA: "I have chosen a king for myself from among his sons"
- **SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS's "provided for Myself" — it captures the divine initiative of *ra'iti* in this context (God has "seen" = "selected/provided") while remaining more natural than EMET's hyper-literal rendering. PNEUMA's "chosen" is too interpretive given that *ra'ah* (to see) is the operative verb.

**16:1** — *Mourning verb*
- EMET: "mourn"
- LOGOS: "mourn"
- PNEUMA: "grieve over"
- **SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "mourn" (EMET/LOGOS consensus). Both are valid for *'aval*, but "mourn" is more formally equivalent.

**16:2** — *Heifer phrasing*
- EMET: "A heifer of the herd take in your hand"
- LOGOS: "Take a heifer with you"
- PNEUMA: "Take a young cow with you"
- **SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS's phrasing. "Heifer" is the standard English rendering of *'eglat baqar*; PNEUMA's "young cow" is needlessly colloquial.

**16:6** — *Samuel's reaction*
- EMET: "and he said, 'Surely before YHWH is His anointed'"
- LOGOS: "he looked upon Eliab and thought, 'Surely the LORD's anointed stands before Him'"
- PNEUMA: "Samuel saw Eliab and thought, 'Surely the LORD's anointed stands here before the LORD'"
- **SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS's rendering. The Hebrew *va-yomer* ("and he said") likely reflects internal speech here; "thought" clarifies this for English readers without distorting the meaning.

**16:7** — *Human perception phrasing*
- EMET: "the man sees to the eyes"
- LOGOS: "man looks upon the outward appearance"
- PNEUMA: "People look at the outward appearance"
- **SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS's phrasing. "Man looks upon the outward appearance" is both clear and formally equivalent. PNEUMA's "People" loses the Hebrew singular. EMET's "sees to the eyes" is too literal for readable English.

**16:11** — *Question about remaining sons*
- EMET: "Are the young men complete?"
- LOGOS: "Are these all the young men?"
- PNEUMA: "Are these all the sons you have?"
- **SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS's phrasing. EMET's "complete" for *tammu* is technically accurate but awkward. PNEUMA's "sons you have" over-interprets. LOGOS balances fidelity and readability.

**16:11** — *What David is doing*
- EMET: "he is shepherding the flock"
- LOGOS: "he is tending the sheep"
- PNEUMA: "he is out tending the sheep"
- **SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS's "tending the sheep." EMET's "shepherding the flock" is slightly more formal but less natural. PNEUMA's added "out" is interpretive.

**16:13** — *Spirit's action*
- EMET: "rushed upon"
- LOGOS: "rushed upon"
- PNEUMA: "came upon David with power"
- **SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "rushed upon" (EMET/LOGOS consensus), which directly translates *tsalchah* and preserves its forceful, sudden quality.

**16:14** — *Evil spirit's effect*
- EMET: "terrified him"
- LOGOS: "tormented him"
- PNEUMA: "terrorized him"
- **SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS's "tormented," which captures the ongoing psychological affliction implied by *bi'atathu* without the extreme violence of "terrorized" or the narrower fear-focus of "terrified."

**16:15** — *Evil spirit description*
- EMET: "an evil spirit of God is terrifying you"
- LOGOS: "an evil spirit from God is tormenting you"
- PNEUMA: "a tormenting spirit from God is troubling you"
- **SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS's rendering. Maintained "evil spirit" (EMET/LOGOS) rather than PNEUMA's "tormenting spirit" — the Hebrew *ruach ra'ah* literally means "evil/bad spirit," and the adjective should be preserved.

**16:16** — *Servant's request phrasing*
- EMET: "Let say, please, our lord, to your servants before you — let them seek a man who is a knower of playing on the lyre"
- LOGOS: "Let our lord now command your servants who are before you to seek out a man who is skilled in playing the lyre"
- PNEUMA: "Let our lord command his servants here before you to search for someone who knows how to play the lyre"
- **SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS's phrasing as the clearest formal rendering.

**16:18** — *David's qualities*
- EMET: "a mighty man of valor and a man of war, and discerning of word, and a man of form"
- LOGOS: "a mighty man of valor, a man of war, prudent in speech, a man of fine appearance"
- PNEUMA: "a brave warrior, a man of war, well-spoken, good-looking"
- **SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS's rendering. "Prudent in speech" best captures *nevon davar*; "a man of fine appearance" preserves the Hebrew construct for *ish to'ar*. PNEUMA's "good-looking" is too casual.

**16:21** — *Saul's affection*
- EMET: "he loved him exceedingly"
- LOGOS: "Saul loved him greatly"
- PNEUMA: "Saul was very fond of him"
- **SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS's "Saul loved him greatly." PNEUMA's "fond of" weakens the Hebrew *va-ye'ehavahu me'od*. EMET's "exceedingly" is slightly archaic.

**16:22** — *Saul's message*
- EMET: "Let stand, please, David before me, for he has found favor in my eyes"
- LOGOS: "Let David remain in my service, for he has found favor in my sight"
- PNEUMA: "Allow David to remain in my service, for I am pleased with him"
- **SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS's rendering with slight adjustment ("sent word to Jesse" from PNEUMA for clarity). "Found favor in my sight" preserves the Hebrew idiom better than PNEUMA's paraphrase.

**16:23** — *Relief description*
- EMET: "there was relief for Saul, and it was good for him"
- LOGOS: "there would be relief for Saul, and it would be well with him"
- PNEUMA: "Saul would find relief and feel better"
- **SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS's phrasing. The iterative "would" correctly captures the Hebrew frequentative construction. "It would be well with him" preserves the Hebrew *tov lo* more faithfully than PNEUMA's "feel better."
